O R D E R

The accused Nos.3 and 4 in C.C. No.191 of 2000 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class - II, Hosdurg filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16(1)
(a) read with Section 2(ia)(j) and 7(i) read with Section 17 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 .
2. Heard.
3.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class - II, Hosdurg
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 20.12.1999 at 5 p.m., PW3, the Food Inspector, purchased 600 gram of banana chips from the shop of the second accused.
First accused was the vendor.
Fourth accused was the manufacturer, who supplied the chips to second accused.
Third accused was the licensee of fourth accused.
After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst.

The report of the Public analyst would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for banana chips under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1956 and therefore, the same was adulterated.
Thereafter, on the request of the accused, second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis.
Ext .P21 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample contained water soluble synthetic colour in violation of Rule 26 of PFA Rules and therefore, it was adulterated.

Thereafter,
complaint was filed before the court by the Food Inspector after complying with the legal formalities.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW6 were examined and Exts. P1 to P29 series were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 was examined and Exts.D1 and D2 were marked for the revision petitioners.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P21 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A)
(ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.

Therefore, Ext. P21 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex Natar Veettil Lakshmi vs State Of Kerala on 12 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197081564/
2 court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra).

entities.text: Apex Natar Veettil Lakshmi vs State Of Kerala on 12 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal.

In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

Even otherwise, in view of the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra), the conviction in this case cannot be sustained as no laboratory was notified and no validated method of analysis was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

In the result, this Revision Petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sec. 16(1)(a) read with Section 2(ia)(j) and 7(i) read with Section 17 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the revision petitioners are acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bonds of the revision petitioners stand cancelled and they are set at liberty.

sd/-
 B.SUDHEENDRA KUMAR,
 JUDGE dl/21.1.2016 // True Copy //
